title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 323/30)
description: The firm is on day 323/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 324/30)
description: The firm is on day 324/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.
signature: replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 324/30)

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 334/30)
description: The firm is on day 334/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.

title: Risk/reward ratio not tracked per position
description: The firm tracks win/loss streak and P&L percentage, but not the risk/reward ratio at entry (potential upside vs downside based on stop-loss and take-profit levels). Over time, a low average R/R ratio erodes profitability even with a high win rate.
auto_fix_hint: At BUY execution, calculate and store `stop_price = entry_price × (1 - STOP_LOSS_PCT)` and `target_price = entry_price × (1 + TAKE_PROFIT_PCT)` in buy_log. Report average R/R in the trade review.

title: SMTP email sends are synchronous and block the pipeline

auto_fix_hint: Wrap email sends in a background thread (threading.Thread) or use asyncio. Store emails in a queue and flush at pipeline end. This would also allow retry on transient SMTP failures.
